title: Joining A.G. Allen: pay and life on the Pullman car
summary: The show was a mile and a half from home; he started at three dollars a week with room and board on the car.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I see. Well, these are all important things to know here. Well, how far did you have to go to join A.G. Allen's Minstrels? When you decided that you were going to leave home, did you have it in mind that you were going to go to A.G. Allen? Or did you just decide to leave and you were going to hook up with...?

When I started... The first minstrel show, which was (?)... The first minstrel show was about...oh, say, about a mile-and-a-half from my home. I could walk there, you know. So I was talkin' with the man, and he said, "You want a job?" I said, "Yeah." He said, "I'll make you my walking gent." When the band goes on parade, if you want to walk beside the drummer and watch him, all right. But when the band comes back off parade, you have to hang those coats up, let them dry. We'll give you the name of the walking gent." He told me how much they'd pay me. I think it... Well, I started at three dollars a week, just to
take care of them coats. And eat and sleep, room and board out on the car.
So you had the Pullman cars.

We had a Pullman car. It was holding(?) I'd say about... Say about a five- or six-piece band and about three chorus girls, and a comedian and a dancer, a soubrette... Of course, the boss, he had his own private office right up in the front, the front of the car, you know.
